label: Peplink MAX BR1 Mini HW3 (LTE-E)
description: Compact mobile router, HW3, EMEA LTE: 3x GE LAN (one convertible to WAN with PrimeCare), 300 Mbps throughput, Wi-Fi, PoE in.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port **0 / 1 (GE)**, Number of Ethernet LAN port **3 / 2 (GE)**, Router Throughput 300 Mbps, Wi-Fi AP Yes, PoE Input Yes, SFP LAN/WAN No. The paired numbers are a licensing effect: with a PrimeCare subscription one LAN port can be turned into a WAN port, giving 1 WAN / 2 LAN instead of 0 WAN / 3 LAN. The base configuration is modelled; **a BR1 Mini with PrimeCare enabled has a different port split from this file.** The **-LTE-E** suffix is the EMEA LTE band set; the ports are identical to the LTEA SKUs, so only the band coverage differs. **PoE: LAN 1 only.** The tech-spec sheet prints "PoE Input Yes [11]" with the footnote "[11] 1x 802.3at PoE" over a three-port LAN row, so it says how many inlets there are but not which socket; the vendor's own hardware reference guide does - the back-panel drawing labels the ports "LAN 1 | 2 | 3 / WAN" and prints **802.3at PoE IN** under LAN 1, with the parts list reading "1x GE LAN Port with 802.3at PoE Input". LAN 1 therefore declares `poeIn: 18` (the datasheet's "Maximum Power Consumption ... 18W", which is what the port has to fund) and LAN 2 / LAN 3 declare `poeIn: false`, because they are not inlets. Sources: https://www.peplink.com/compare/tech-specs/br1-mini.pdf (tech-spec sheet: PoE class, "1x 802.3at PoE", and "Nominal Power Consumption 13W" / "Maximum Power Consumption 18W") and https://download.peplink.com/manual/br1_mini_hw3_hardware_reference_guide.pdf (panel drawing and parts list, LAN 1).
